newsitem.title: USA: PG&E gains CPUC approval on spending plan.
newsitem.headline: PG&E gains CPUC approval on spending plan.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission on Friday approved a plan by Pacific Gas and Electric Co to increase spending on transmission and distribution reliability.

Under state legislation passed earlier this year, customer electricity rates are frozen, but the utility will be able to shift about $160 million of base revenues out of capital depreciation payments.
"This is a redistribution of revenues," PG&E spokesman Bill Sessa said. "We will spend less on capital retirement."

Under the state plan, utilities will eventually make back capital investments in assets that are expected to become uneconomic under market competition through a "competitive transition charge" levied on customer bills.
The exact amount of the transition charge is to be determined later next year after apublic hearings.
"This is a policy decision to emphasize reliability," noted Sessa.
